naming_clarity.reason: Plain stakeholder language (remaining charge, capacity lost, predicted range, fleet report, calibrated bench, everyday middle of its range) with no abbreviations; remaining capacity is explained in the body as what is left of the original capacity.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: Names no implementation constructs; it states what is shown and measured, not how charge or capacity is estimated (no counting method, filter, voltage correction or memory).

parent_fit.reason: Root of the V: the user_stories stage has no upstream stage (depends_on is empty) and the story has no outgoing trace link, so there is no parent to engage with and the axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: The title, the I-want clause and the so-that clause each name two outcomes with different purposes and observers: reporting the remaining charge (trust the predicted range; shown by the vehicle and checked on a bench) and reporting the capacity lost (plan pack replacement; shown in the fleet report); either could ship without the other, and the graph already gives the capacity figure its own component (a capacity-fade tracker) apart from the charge estimators, so this covers two independently deliverable capabilities.
single_user_capability.suggestion: Split into a remaining-charge story (accuracy, no jump across switch-off and switch-on, reliability indication) and a remaining-capacity story (the reported figure never rises), each tracing its own requirements.

user_observable.reason: Three concrete observables with named observers: the charge level the vehicle shows does not jump across a switch-off and switch-on, the remaining-capacity figure in the fleet report never rises, and a workshop bench discharge compares every mid-range reported charge level with the charge that actually came out.

summary: Concretely observable and plain-language, but it bundles two independently deliverable capabilities (remaining charge and remaining capacity) that should be separate stories.
